title: A Scotch Haggis
description: A boiled, filled haggis casing with finely minced meat and offal, grated liver, suet, onions and dried meal. Stock moistens the mixture, while mixed spices season the rich, coarse-textured filling.
steps: Make the haggis bag perfectly clean
Parboil the drought, boil the liver very well, so as it will grate, dry the meat before the fire
Mince the drought and a pretty large piece of beef very small
Grate about half the liver
Mince plenty of the suet and some onions small
Mix all these ingredients very well together, with a handful or two of the dried meal
Spread them on the table, and season them properly with salt and mixed spices
Take any of the scraps of beef that is left from mincing, and some of the water that boiled the drought, and make about a chopin (i.e., a quart) of good stock of it
Put all the haggis meat into the bag, and that broth in it
Sew the bag, but be sure to put out all the wind, before you sew it quite close
If you think the bag is thin, you may put it in a cloth
If it is a large haggis, it will take at least two hours boiling

description: Stuffed veal is gently stewed with onion, mace and parsley, then served with its strained cooking liquor enriched with egg yolks and lemon juice. The pale, savory sauce can also include mushrooms or celery.

description: Veal sweetbreads are simmered with stock and vegetables, sliced, and coated with an egg-enriched lemon white sauce. The chilled pieces are skewered, breaded and fried, giving a crisp exterior around the tender sweetbreads.

Add one onion, one carrot, one turnip, two bay-leaves, and a pint of stock

When cold, run the skewer through the pieces, putting several on each skewer
Dip them into egg well beaten, then into bread crumbs
Fry in hot lard
Serve on a napkin

steps: Mix two parts of fine flour of pale barley malt with one part of wheat flour

title: Simple butter-baked apples
description: Whole apples bake until tender around a small butter-and-sugar filling. Their juices collect in the dish, making a light sauce to spoon over the warm fruit.

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Wash {{item-0}}. Remove the cores from the stem end, leaving the bottom intact.
Set the apples upright in a snug oven-safe dish. Divide {{item-1}} and {{item-2}} evenly among the core openings. Pour {{item-3}} around the apples.
Bake for 35–50 minutes, until a small knife slips easily into the flesh. If the dish dries out, add a splash of hot water.
Let stand for 5 minutes. Serve one apple per portion, with the pan juices spooned over.

title: Baked Bream And Egg Sauce
description: Bream baked with lemon juice, coated in white sauce and decorated with hard-boiled egg, parsley and lemon slices.
steps: Wash the bream, rub some dripping on to a baking sheet, lay on it the fish, squeeze over a few drops of lemon juice; cover with a piece of paper well rubbed with dripping, and bake in a moderate oven for about twenty minutes or longer, if the fish is large.
Remove the skin and fins, and put them on the dish; pour over the white sauce, which should be just thick enough to coat the fish.
Chop the parsley finely, and boil the egg hard, cut it in half, and either chop the yolk or rub it through a sieve, and chop the white.
Arrange these in alternate rows all over the fish, and garnish with a few lemon slices.

title: Baked Fish
description: Layers of boned fish and lemon-herb breadcrumb seasoning, baked with butter beneath a crumb topping.
steps: Split open the fish and remove the head and backbone, wash well in cold water and dry in a cloth.
Chop the parsley, herbs, and suet, and mix these together; add half the crumbs, the rind of half a lemon, and pepper and salt.
Butter a baking tin, lay on a fish skin downwards.
On this place a layer of seasoning, a little lemon juice, and a few pieces of butter; on this another fish with the cut part next the seasoning.
Do the rest in the same way, piling one on top of another; over all put the rest of the crumbs and butter, bake in a moderate oven for half an hour.
Slip into a hot dish, and serve.

title: Berlin, White, or Pale Beer (Wess-bier)
description: A wheat-dominant beer brewed with barley malt and hops, then fermented with top yeast.

ingredients.name: Water at 95°F., thirty quarts per scheffel of malt
ingredients.sourceText: Water at 95°F., thirty quarts per scheffel of malt

ingredients.name: Half a pound of Altmark hops per bushel of malt

steps: Mingle the barley malt and wheat malt together, then moisten and crush between rollers
Work up the mixture with water at 95°F., in the proportion of thirty quarts per scheffel of malt
Add seventy quarts of boiling water to the pasty mixture
Mash the whole in the tun
Leave it a little to settle
Draw off a portion of the thin liquor by the tap and transfer to the copper
Add to it a decoction of half a pound of Altmark hops, separately prepared, for each bushel of malt
After half an hour's boiling, turn the hopped wort back with the hops into the mash-tun, of which the temperature should now be 162°F., but not more
In half an hour draw the wort from off the grains and pump into the cooler
Afterwards mash the grains with from forty to fifty quarts of boiling water per scheffel of malt
Draw off this infusion and add to the former malt
Set the whole mixture at 66°F. with a due proportion of top yeast or ordinary barm
Ferment very moderately

title: Bola d'Amor
description: A layered almond, citron and sweet egg-thread confection, shaped into a cone and gently baked to set the surface.
steps: Clarify {{source-0}}
To ascertain when it is of proper consistency, drop a spoonful in cold water, form it into a ball, and try if it sounds when struck against a glass
Take the yolks of twenty eggs, mix them up gently, and pass them through a sieve
Have ready a funnel, the hole of which must be about the size of a vermicelli
Hold the funnel over the sugar while it is boiling over a charcoal fire
Pour the egg through, stirring the sugar all the time, and taking care to hold the funnel at such a distance from the sugar as to admit of the egg dripping into it
When the egg has been a few minutes in the sugar, it will be hard enough to take out with a silver fork, and place on a drainer
Continue adding egg to the boiling sugar till enough is obtained
Prepare {{source-2}} finely pounded and boiled in sugar, clarified with orange rose-water only
Place in a dish a layer of this paste, over which place a layer of citrons cut in thin slices, and then a thick layer of the egg prepared as above
Continue working thus in alternate layers till high enough to look handsome
Pile in the form of a cone, with the egg forming the last layer
Place in a gentle oven till it becomes a little set, and the last layer slightly crisp
Serve in the dish in which it is baked
Ornament with myrtle and gold and silver leaf

title: Choux Pastry
description: Small baked choux made from cooked butter-and-flour paste enriched with eggs, then opened and filled with sweetmeats.
steps: Let the butter, sugar, salt, and lemon peel boil until the whole is properly melted
Take some very dry flour and pass through a sieve
Take the lemon-peel out with a ladle, and throw a handful of flour into the preparation while boiling, taking care not to put more flour than the liquor can soak up
Stir with a wooden spoon until the paste can be easily detached from the stewpan, and then take it off the fire
Break an egg into this paste, and mix it well; then break a second, which also mix
Do not put more eggs than the paste can absorb, but be careful not to make this preparation too liquid
Form them en choux, in the shape of a ball, an inch in circumference
Dress the choux on a baking-sheet, at an inch distance from each other
Brush them over with egg-wash to which has been added a little milk
Put them into an oven moderately hot, but do not open the oven till they are quite baked
Dry them, and sometimes you may glaze them, or not
To detach them from the baking-sheet, apply the sharp end of a knife, and take them off gently
Make a small opening in the side of the choux, into which put with a tea-spoon such sweetmeats as you think proper, and serve them dished en buisson

title: Cobbett's Yeast Cakes
description: Dried bread-starter cakes made from hop infusion, rye flour and cornmeal, rehydrated before use in a bread sponge.

ingredients.name: Indian corn meal
ingredients.sourceText: seven pounds of Indian corn meal

ingredients.name: three and a half pounds of rye flour
ingredients.sourceText: three and a half pounds of rye flour

steps: Separate the hops by the hand, strew and boil them in the water for half an hour
Strain the liquor into an earthen vessel
Put in the rye while hot, stirring quickly as the fermentation commences
Next day, when it is working, put in the Indian meal, stirring it well
Knead it well, and roll it out as you would a pie-crust, to the thickness of the third of an inch
Cut it into cakes with a tumbler
Place these cakes in the sun to dry
Turn them every day until they are hard
Keep them in a dry place
When you bake, take a couple of these cakes, break them and put them into warm water over-night
Let the vessel containing them stand near the fire; they will dissolve
Use the liquid for setting your sponge, just as you would the yeast of beer

title: Cock-A-Leekie Soup
description: A slow-simmered soup of giblets and leeks, with peppercorns and optional bacon rind for flavor.
steps: Wash and slice up the leeks into pieces about one inch long
Put them into a saucepan with the butter or dripping made thoroughly hot
Cover over and let them cook for half an hour, stirring occasionally
While they are cooking clean the giblets thoroughly, washing them first in hot and then in cold water
Cut open the gizzard, remove the stones, and cleanse well
Cut them all up into small pieces and put them into the saucepan with the leeks
Pour over the boiling water or liquor
Put in the peppercorns tied in a piece of muslin, and a piece of bacon rind if there is any in the larder
Let it simmer slowly for three hours
If not brown enough add a few drops of caramel
Take out the peppercorns and bacon rind
Season to taste
Pour into a hot tureen and serve

description: A cold molded preparation of cooked eel, hard-boiled egg and parsley, set in its strained cooking broth with gelatin.
steps: Clean the eels, cut them into pieces 2 inches long
Put them in cold water well seasoned with salt, 2 dozen peppercorns and the vegetables, and a spoonful of vinegar
Bring to the boil, and skim well
Boil steadily for an hour, or longer if the eels are large
Take out the fish, slip out the bones, and cut the meat into small pieces

Strain the liquor over and stand away till cold
Turn out and serve with a salad

description: A plain yeast bread made through an initial sponge, kneaded into a stiff dough and divided into loaves for baking.

ingredients.name: one quarter of a pint of good yeast

steps: Put fourteen pounds of flour into a pan
Add to one quart of warm water a quarter of a pint of good yeast
Make a hole in the flour, pour in the water and the yeast
Stir it well with a wooden spoon until it forms a thickish paste
Throw a little flour over, and leave it in a warm place
In about an hour when it has risen and burst through the covering of flour, add more warm water and three teaspoonfuls of salt
Knead until it forms a rather stiff dough, working it as much as possible
Let it remain, covered with a cloth, for an hour
Divide it into loaves
Bake for an hour and a quarter
